Sam (CS): @Aishwarya quick ping — onboarding for Orchid Labs. Mobile SDK (iOS v0.9.3) sees intermittent 429s after a few minutes of activity. They only get 429s from specific EU region. Any quick checks? :wave:
Aishwarya (SDK Eng): Hi Sam — can you paste a short client log and the auth token rotation timing?
Sam (CS): Sure. customer says tokens rotate every 30s, they use websocket keepalive, and they call preflight on each app resume. Logs:
```
[2026-03-20T14:02:11Z] POST /v1/chat 200 OK latency=120ms
[2026-03-20T14:02:13Z] preflight token-refresh ok ttl=30s
[2026-03-20T14:02:15Z] POST /v1/chat 429 Too Many Requests region=eu-west1
[2026-03-20T14:02:16Z] retry backoff=0.5s
[2026-03-20T14:02:45Z] preflight token-refresh ok ttl=30s
[2026-03-20T14:02:46Z] POST /v1/chat 429 Too Many Requests region=eu-west1
```
Sam (CS): They said steady traffic ~3 req/s per device (background sync + user actions), ~200 devices in early tests.
Miguel (DevEx): Hmm repeating token refresh + preflight per resume could cause head-of-line fanout to auth/edge. Also TTL 30s is pretty aggressive. Is Orchid using ephemeral tokens from our console or self-managed refresh?
Orchid-Dev (customer): We implemented ephemeral via our backend using /token-exchange and set client refresh 30s to keep sessions short for security. We also saw most 429s spike shortly after release when many devices resumed at similar times.
Aishwarya (SDK Eng): Two angles: client-side splay + exponential jitter on preflight, and server-side rate-windowing. For immediate workaround set client refresh to 120s and add random jitter 0-10s on refresh schedule. Also please check that preflight is skipped if websocket already has a valid conn/kvcache.
Sam (CS): Orchid can we try 120s TTL and splay? Want to test a quick config change before we escalate.
Orchid-Dev (customer): Ok doing that now. We can push an internal build via staged rollout to 10% of devices.
infra-bot: Note: observed short-term auth service spike at 2026-03-20T14:02:10Z - routing to eu-west1 saturated for 90s. Auto-failover did not trigger due to sticky region rule.
Miguel (DevEx): That sticky region rule is likely why only eu-west1 saw 429s. If devices pin to region on onboarding, a splay will help, but we should also relax sticky routing for short-lived tokens — I’ll open infra ticket.
Aishwarya (SDK Eng): For reproducer: can Orchid run a small load test from EU with tokens rotating at 30s and preflight on every resume? If yes, collect a pcap or sample HTTP header X-Request-ID and we can trace on our side.
Orchid-Dev (customer): We ran the staged build with 120s + splay. In 20 mins the 429 rate dropped from ~7% to 0.4% on the 10% cohort. Will ramp to 50% if stable.
Sam (CS): Awesome, thanks. Can Miguel add a temporary infra rule to allow cross-region fallback when auth TTL < 60s? That would reduce impact for customers who insist on short token life.
Miguel (DevEx): Yup I’ll create INFRA-5621 and tag infra-oncall. Proposed short-term: override sticky-region for token-rotate-age < 60s and short-circuit to nearest healthy region. Long-term we’ll add token-age metadata to routing.
Aishwarya (SDK Eng): Also sending a small SDK patch to change preflight semantics: if websocket connection state == OPEN and KV cache fresh (<10s) skip preflight. Will post PR and release notes.
Sam (CS): Filing a follow-up doc for onboarding playbook changes (reduce default ephemeral refresh to 90–180s, always splay, doc preflight best practices).
Orchid-Dev (customer): Thanks all — ramping to 50% now. Will report after 60m. :thumbsup:
Sam (CS): Marking this thread as resolved if 50% cohort stays healthy — please ping if 429s reappear.
Aishwarya (SDK Eng): quick checklist for internal: 1) confirm infra ticket 2) backtrace sample X-Request-IDs 3) SDK PR publish 4) update onboarding doc.
Miguel (DevEx): INFRA-5621 created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-5621 — tagging infra-oncall and eng-runtime.
Orchid-Dev (customer): Update: 50% roll complete, 429s at 0.6% and trending down. We'll do full rollout tomorrow morning.
Sam (CS): Great. Capturing lessons learned for renewal risk: early spike was mitigated; recommend scheduling a 30-min enablement call to walkthrough safe defaults to avoid churn.
Aishwarya (SDK Eng): noted — will join the enablement call.
Sam (CS): Closing thread in 24h after final rollout. Thanks everyone!
